title: OU's First Rose Bowl: 34-14 Over Washington State in 2003
question: When did Oklahoma first play in the Rose Bowl?
answer: Oklahoma's first Rose Bowl was on January 1, 2003, when Bob Stoops' No. 8 Sooners beat No. 7 Washington State 34-14 in Pasadena. Quarterback Nate Hybl was named the game's MVP.
summary: Oklahoma's first Rose Bowl came on Jan. 1, 2003, a 34-14 win over Washington State. Nate Hybl was MVP and OU's defense held the Cougars to 4 rushing yards.
body: For all its bowl history, Oklahoma had never played in Pasadena until the 2002 season. As the Associated Press noted, it was the Sooners' 36th bowl game but their first Rose Bowl. The door opened when the Orange Bowl selected Iowa and USC, leaving the Rose Bowl without its usual Pac-10 versus Big Ten pairing. Big 12 champion Oklahoma got the call to face Washington State.

The Sooners took command late in the first half. After an early field goal, Nate Hybl threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Antwone Savage, and Antonio Perkins followed with a 51-yard punt return touchdown for a 17-0 lead. A third-quarter field goal and Hybl's 9-yard scoring pass to Curtis Fagan pushed the margin to 27-0 before Washington State scored in the final six minutes. Quentin Griffin added a 19-yard touchdown run and finished with 144 yards on 30 carries, his 10th straight 100-yard game.

The defense set the tone. A Cougar offense that had averaged nearly 35 points was held to a season-low 243 yards and just 4 rushing yards, and star quarterback Jason Gesser was sacked six times and intercepted twice. Hybl, in his final college game, went 19 of 29 for 240 yards and two touchdowns without an interception.
The victory completed a 12-2 season. Oklahoma would not return to the Rose Bowl for 15 years, when it met Georgia there in a College Football Playoff semifinal.
